- Date issued: 11 August 2026 (page 2 signature date; the certificate revision 2 date). Page 1 doesn't have an explicit issue date but page 2 has "Date: 11 August 2026". Also revision history shows Addition 2 on 11 August 2026.

Page total: 8 pages
OIML issuer ID: "V 3112" appears as a logo/emblem identifier — that might be the CMI notified body number 3112? Actually "V 3112" is likely a logo. Hmm, oiml_issuer_id — not clear. The certificate number R49/2013-A-CZ1-25.01 suggests CZ1. The "V 3112" is probably the EC type-examination certificate style mark. I'll not fabricate; maybe omit oiml_issuer_id or leave it out since unclear. Actually, scheme A certificates don't have issuer IDs typically. I'll omit.

- Type evaluation report No. 0511-ER-V163-24 revision 1 dated 26 May 2026, 36 pages including annex 1, role: type_evaluation_report
- Documentation file: 0511-UL-V163-24, role: documentation_file

Revision history:
- Addition 0, 10 January 2025, Issuing certificate
- Addition 1, 15 December 2025, Addition new ratio R500 and new dimensions DN 32 – DN 40
- Addition 2, 11 August 2026, Typo errors in lengths for DN25 and DN40

Note revision field: "0", "1", "2" as strings. The table says "Addition 0" etc. I'll use "0", "1", "2".

Footnotes:
- "1) The ratio Q₃ / Q₁ shall be chosen according to paragraph 4.1.4 of OIML R 49-1:2013" — Actually the markdown shows `<sup>1</sup> The ratio Q₃ / Q₁ shall be chosen...` with markers `1` on "Mechanical environment class" and "Electromagnetic environment". Hmm wait, footnote text says "The ratio Q3/Q1 shall be chosen according to paragraph 4.1.4..." That doesn't match mechanical environment class... but it's what's in the document. Actually the superscript 1 appears on both "Mechanical environment class (OIML R 49-1:2013/ Directive 2014/32/EU): 1" and "Electromagnetic environment: 1". The footnote text seems mismatched but I record what's there. Footnote marker "1" with that text.

- There's also `<sup>2</sup>` on "Power supply (Umax / Imax)2:" but no footnote definition for 2. So only record the footnote for 1.

Model family: The certificate covers nominal diameters 15, 20, 25, 32, 40 (DN15–DN40). This is a family of 5 models.

Characteristics:
Per-DN (model_level):
- nominal_diameter: 15, 20, 25, 32, 40 (mm implied — "[DN]" not given unit, but nominal diameter typically mm). The table header says "Nominal diameter:" with values 15, 20, 25 / 32, 40. Unit not explicitly given. I could use unit_symbol "mm" — hmm, rule 8 says don't fabricate. Nominal diameter DN15 means 15 mm... The markdown gives no unit. Safer: unit_symbol null. Actually DN is dimensionless-ish designation. I'll leave unit_symbol null.

- length_mm: 165, 190, 225 for DN15, 20, 25; 230, 245 for DN32, 40. Attribute "length", unit "mm". Footnote: revision 2 fixed typo errors in lengths for DN25 and DN40 — not footnotes though.

- pressure_loss_class: Δp63 (DN15), Δp40 (DN20), Δp25 (DN25); Δp63 for DN32 and 40. This is a code value, string. Model level: DN15 → "Δp63", DN20 → "Δp40", DN25 → "Δp25", DN32 → "Δp63", DN40 → "Δp63".

- connection_type: G¾"B, G1"B, G1 ¼"B (DN15, 20, 25); G1½"B, G2"B (DN32, 40). String values. Could be model_level.

Common (type_level):
- q3_q1_ratio: 250; 400; 500 → This is a list of allowed ratio values. Rule: "Lists of values" should be model matrix if varying by model, but here it's a common set of options for all models. Hmm. R49 uses ratio Q3/Q1 as a selection. The certificate covers ratios 250, 400, 500. This could be a config axis... But the model variations are by DN and ratio. The flowrate table (Basic metrological data) got cut off, so we don't have per-ratio flowrates. 

I think best: record as a type-level characteristic with value as... rule says lists of values is a MODEL MATRIX when it's multiple Emax values per field. Here it's "Q3/Q1: 250; 400; 500" meaning the ratio can be one of these. Since all models share the same set, I could record it as a single value string "250; 400; 500" or as config_level. Hmm.

Rule 4 says: "Lists of values. 25,30,50,60,75,90 (multiple Emax values) is a MODEL MATRIX — emit model_level entries, NOT a list-as-value." For Emax, each value = a different model. Here, ratio 250/400/500 doesn't create distinct models in the same sense — but it does create variants. The models could be identified as DN + ratio. But the flowrate table is truncated so we can't populate per-ratio data.

Given the doc, models by DN is the primary matrix. For ratio, I could add config_level entries: attribute "q3_q1_ratio", axis... no, config_level is for attribute × config-axis matrix with values {condition, value}. Here it's one attribute with three allowed values across all models. 

Option: record `q3_q1_ratio` as type-level with value {min:250, max:500}? No — that's wrong, it's a discrete set, not a range.

Option: emit a model_level? No — models are DN-based.

I think emitting a characteristic with a list value is cleanest, but schema says value must be number|{min,max}|string. I could use value string "250; 400; 500". Hmm, but strict rule says lists of values → model matrix. However the model axis is DN, not ratio. Alternatively, treat each ratio as a config condition:

config_level: [
  {attribute: "q3_q1_ratio", axis: "ratio_selection", values: [{condition: "available_ratio_1", value: 250}, ...]}
]

That's clunky. I think the most faithful approach given the truncated flowrate table: models = DN15, DN20, DN25, DN32, DN40 with attributes; and record q3_q1_ratio as a type-level value string "250/400/500" — hmm.

Actually, let me reconsider: maybe make model_id include both DN and note that ratio selection 250–500 is shared. I'll record q3_q1_ratio_allowed_values as a type-level characteristic with value as string "250; 400; 500". Hmm, but rule 2 STRICT... "Lists of values ... is a MODEL MATRIX". 

Alternative: treat ratio as a config axis where condition = ratio value itself and value = null? No.

Let me think about what best serves downstream parsing. The R49 flowrate table (truncated) would give Q1..Q4 per DN per ratio. Since it's truncated, we can't do the full matrix. I'll emit a matrix_table for the truncated table? The table is cut off — only header rows "Manufacturer" and "Model number:" with colspan=12. Not useful content. I'll skip it.

Decision: I'll put "q3_q1_ratio" in type_level with value string "250; 400; 500". Hmm... Actually, maybe better: since the certificate's revision 1 added "new ratio R500", the ratio is a genuine variant axis. I could define models as DN × ratio combos = 15 models. That's overkill without flowrate data.

Compromise: model_family models = 5 DNs. characteristics.model_level includes nominal_diameter, length, pressure_loss_class, connection_type. characteristics.config_level: attribute "q3_q1_ratio", axis "metrological ratio selection", values [{condition: "ratio", value: 250}, {condition:"ratio", value:400}, {condition:"ratio", value:500}]? That's awkward too.

Simplest defensible: type_level entry with value "250; 400; 500" as string... but rule 2 forbids? It says lists of values is a model matrix. Strictly following the rule for "250,30,..." example. But here the list isn't per-model; it's a set of allowed ratios common to all models. The example rule context: "25,30,50,60,75,90 (multiple Emax values)" — Emax varying → models. Ratio choices don't map to the DN model axis.

I'll go with type_level: q3_q1_ratio with value string "250; 400; 500". Hmm, but maybe better to normalize: value {min:250, max:500}? No — discrete.

Actually, you know, I could do config_level properly: axis = "Q3/Q1 ratio selection", and values = [{condition: "R250", value: 250}, {condition: "R400", value: 400}, {condition: "R500", value: 500}]. The "value" being the ratio. That captures it as a config axis. I think that's reasonable per rule 5. But is it necessary? The schema allows it. I'll do that... Actually wait — config_level's typical use: attribute × config-axis matrix where the attribute value depends on configuration. Here the "attribute" is the ratio itself. Meh.

I'll keep it simple and faithful: type_level "q3_q1_ratio_options" hmm.

Let me just go with type_level:
- "q3_q1_ratio": {value: "250 / 400 / 500", unit_symbol: null}

Hmm, rule 10... no. Let me reconsider once more. The strict rule intent: don't lose multi-value info as a string when it indicates a model family. Here we already have model_family captured by DN. The ratio list is a shared characteristic. I'll use string value. Fine.

- q4_q3_ratio: 1.25
- measuring_principle: "ultrasonic"
- accuracy_class: 2
- temperature_class: "T50; T30" → list again. Temperature classes T50 and T30 (max admissible temp 50°C and 30°C). Record as string "T50; T30" or two? I'll record as string. Or could be config... The "Maximum admissible temperature" is 50 °C (the higher class). Actually max admissible temperature [°C]: 50. So temperature_class T50/T30 options; MAT = 50°C. I'll record temperature_class value "T50; T30" as string.
- water_pressure_class: "MAP16"

- mechanical_environment_class: "B, O / M1" (R49-1 / MID). Footnote marker 1. Record value string "B, O / M1", footnote_markers ["1"]. Hmm the footnote 1 text is about Q3/Q1 ratio... mismatched, but rule says record marker when value references footnote. The sup 1 is attached to those rows. I'll include marker "1". Hmm, footnote_markers format — the schema example shows ["1)"]. The markdown shows <sup>1</sup>. I'll use "1".  Actually rule 7 example: {"value": ..., "footnote_markers": ["1)"]}. The footnote definition begins with `<sup>1</sup>`. I'll use "1".
